texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147169043/ 1 1. The present complaint has been filed by the complainant U/s 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband and in laws. Respondent no. 1 is the husband and other respondents are in laws of the complainant. The brief facts of the case as disclosed in the complaint are that the marriage between the complainant and respondent no.1 was solemnized on 10.11.2011 at Beawer, Rajasthan according to Hindu Rites and Ceremonies. 2. It is further stated that the marriage between the complainant and respondent no. 1 was settled on account of the respondent no. 5, who is the cousin brother of the respondent no. 1. The respondent no. 5 had visited alongwith some Jain Saint in the vicinity where the complainant with her family has been residing and the respondent no. 5 was deputed for the care and welfare of the said Jain Saint with other boys. The complainant and her mother used to visit for ' Darshan" of the said Jain Saint, where CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 2/15 they met the respondent no. 5 and persuaded the complainant's mother by offering that the respondent no. 1 is his cousin and belongs to very good family and has very handsome income and thereafter they sent the photograph of the respondent no. 1 for meeting. The parents and brother thus visited the house of the respondent no. 1 where they were given welcome and by using undue influence and compulsion got fixed the marriage between the complainant and respondent no. 1. They told that they do not want anything in the dowry except marriage to be performed in good manner. They also said that they have everything with them and they do not want anything from the parents of the complainant. 3. It is further stated that however thereafter the respondents started forcing and compelling the complainant for early marriage and they of their own fixed the date of marriage i.e. 10.11.2011 without any consultation with the parents of the complainant. The parents of the complainant had no other option but accept the same as they could not understand the bad intentions of the respondents. It is further stated that after fixing the date of marriage, the respondents started their modus operandi and making one after another demand from the parents of the complainant. They started saying before marriage that the parents of the complainant would give gold ring and chain and wrist watch for the boy and further how much cash will be given in the marriage and that they have to show and give cash to their relatives. They also demanded gold tops for the maternal grand mother of the boy. 4. It is further stated the parents of the complainant due to demands and pressure of the respondents spent huge amount in the marriage and gave very handsome dowry articles which includes the gold jewelery ornaments, electrical appliances, furniture, utensils and household articles, clothes etc. It is further stated that after the marriage, the respondents brought the complainant to their house, where the marriage was duly consummated between the parties. It is further stated that immediately after the marriage when the complainant was brought at the said house by the respondent no. 1 and in laws, they showed their dissatisfaction with the CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 3/15 dowry articles brought by her in the marriage. The respondent no. 1 alongwith other respondents told that her father has not given them enough dowry articles like more jewelery ornaments. Therefore, right from the beginning all Cc No. 59/1/12 Ps: Subzi Mandi Kritika ... vs . Ankit Jain 1/15 on 18 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147169043/ 2 respondents started harassing, illtreating, humiliating the complainant for not fulfilling their demands. It was given specific threat to her that in case she did not fulfill their demands they will not allow her to live peacefully at their house and will ruin her life. 5. It is further stated that since the complainant belongs to a respectable family and since after the marriage, it was obligatory on her part being morally, socially and legally to discharge her marital obligations as a devoted Hindu Wedded wife and it was the lesson given by her parents and other relatives to live and bear even in odd circumstances and therefore she thought that after passing of time, the accused and in laws would change their behaviour and attitude towards her and she would also lead a happy married life with them. It is further stated that immediately after the marriage, the complainant started doing the household work so that she may be able to win over the heart and minds of the accused and in laws as they were not happy and satisfied with the dowry articles brought by her. But unfortunately despite her selfless efforts, the respondents did not appreciate. 6. It is further stated that when the complainant and her parents could not fulfill the demands of the respondents, they started torturing, beating and inflicting mental and physical cruelties upon the complainant. Immediately after the marriage, the respondents took all the jewelery ornaments from her on the pretext that because of huge rush of relatives in the house there could be chance of stealing of the jewelery ornaments and he will keep the same safely. 7. It is further stated that after 45 days of the marriage, the respondent no. 3 and 4 started torturing, harassing and beating to the complainant while the respondents no. 1 and 2 used to remain spectator. It is further stated that respondents used to say that the complainant has to get fulfilled their demands if she wants to live in their house. The respondents no. 3 and 4 also uttered that in their family already one daughter in law has been burnt alive, other daughter in law has been killed by giving CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 4/15 poison and the third is being beaten up daily. They terrorized and warned the complainant that if she want to live comfortably the she has to fulfill their demands. They used to make demand of cash and fixed deposit and jewelery ornaments. 8. It is further stated that the complainant was not allowed to even talk to her parents or any other relations and whenever the parents of th complainant made telephone call, the respondents no. 3 and 4 used to say that the complainant is living very happily and she even does not remember them once. It is further stated that the complainant tolerated all the cruel treatment of the respondent no. 1 and other in laws with a hope that better sense will prevail upon them because the complainant became pregnant and she thought that after birth of child her life became normal an she will be given respect by the respondent no. 1 and his other family members, but all the hopes and expectations of the complainant ruined. 9. It is further stated that the complainant was regularly beaten and tortured by the respondent no. 1 at the instance of other family members and he used to beat her blue and black. The respondent no. 1 is a habitual drinker and he used to beat the complainant like animals. At many occasions, the respondent no. 1 at the instructions of the other in laws even tried to kill her by strangulate. These mental and physical torture by the respondent no. 1 totally broken up the complainant and she Cc No. 59/1/12 Ps: Subzi Mandi Kritika ... vs . Ankit Jain 1/15 on 18 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147169043/ 3 became pale and weak as she was not provided with proper food and diet. The respondent no.1 warned her that in case his demands of Rs. 5,00,000/ cash is not get fulfilled by the complainant from her parents he will make her life a hell and miserable. 10. It is further stated that thereafter the respondents hatched a conspiracy and the respondent no. 1 brought the complainant to her parents on 7 th February, 2012 and after leaving her there, the respondent no. 1 went back giving threats tht in cas she will not get fulfilled their said demands of Rs. 5,00,000/ cash as well as jewelery ornaments as per demand of his mother, sister and father she will not be taken back to her matrimonial home. It is further stated that since then the complainant lis living at her parents house and all the efforts and persuasion by the complainant and CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 5/15 her parents yield no fruitful result and on the other hand the respondent no. 1 himself as well as respondent no. 3 used to telephone to the complainant and her parents whether their demands are fulfilled or not and till their demands are not met they will not take back the complainant to her parental home. The respondent no. 3 has further threatened that if the said demands are not fulfilled immediately then they will get the respondent no. 1 remarried with some other girl as they are getting many offers who are ready to give handsome dowry articles and cash. 11. It is further stated that the respondents have also threatened to kill the complainant as well as her family members in case she makes any complaint against them to the police. The complainant also made a complaint dated 12.03.2012 with the SHO PS Subzi Mandi, Delhi. It is further stated that due to merciless beatings, torture, keeping the complainant hungry and providing no proper medical aid and other need during the pregnancy and this has resulted into deteriorating the health of the complainant and her parents therefore, took her to the hospital an d the doctors opined that the pregnancy of the complainant has been in quite danger which is dangerous to the own life of the complainant as there was bleeding and severe pain in her abdomen and lastly due to miscarriage the pregnancy was terminated and the complainant was admitted at Aggarwal Dharmarth Hospital, Shakti Nagar, Delhi from 16.03.2012 and discharged on 18.03.2012 and despite information neither the respondent nor other in laws came and they told that they do not bother whether the complainant dies or alive. 12. It is further stated that the complainant continued to suffer all the atrocities and torture of the respondents with the hope that the respondents would mend their behaviour and conduct and she will live a peaceful life at the matrimonial home but of no use. It is further stated that all the dowry/istridhan articles including the jewelery ornaments and other valuables of the complainant are in the custody of the respondents, who are misappropriating the same and have refused to return the same to the complainant and are repeatedly threatening her and her family members. It is further stated that the complainant has always compromised and CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 6/15 tolerated all atrocities of the respondent no. 1 and in laws to save her marital life with dignity and honor. But the respondent no. 1 and in laws have never showed any love, affection and interest with the complainant. 13. It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 has also not made any provision for the maintenance of the complainant. The respondent no. 1 is enjoying very comfortable life as he is running his Cc No. 59/1/12 Ps: Subzi Mandi Kritika ... vs . Ankit Jain 1/15 on 18 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147169043/ 4 business of artificial jewelery and is earning Rs. 1,00,000/ per month. He owns various properties, bank balance. He has no other liability except to maintain the complainant. It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 has not made any provisions for complainant's maintenance and therefore, complainant is left with no other option but to seek the relief and legal remedy from this Hon'ble Court hence this petition. 14. The following orders have been requested to be passed : (i) Protection Order Under Section 18 : (a) prohibiting the respondents from any form of communication including personal, oral or written or electronic or telephonic contact with the complainant, (b) prohibiting alienation of istridhan articles of the complainant, shared household and other properties in the name of the respondents, ( c) directing the respondents to stay away from the complainant and her relatives and to prohibit commission of violence against them. (ii) Residence Order Under Section 19: (a) directing the respondent no.1 to pay the rent, electricity and water bills @ Rs. 10,000/ per month for alternative residential accommodation and allow the complainant to visit and live at the matrimonial home, (b) restraining the respondents from causing any obstruction to the complainant from entering the portion of the shared household in which she wants to reside, (c) entitling the complainant to have continued access to her personal effects situated at shared household, (d) directing the respondent no. 1 to secure same level of alternate accommodation or to pay rent in lieu of alternate accommodation, CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 7/15 (iii) Monetary Relief Under Section 20: (a) directing the respondents either to return all istridhan articles as per the list attached or compensate for the amount of istridhan including cash taken till date i.e. total Rs. 10,00,000/, istridhan articles worth Rs. 3,00,000/ given to husband and in laws @ 13,00,000/, Cc No. 59/1/12 Ps: Subzi Mandi Kritika ... vs . Ankit Jain 1/15 on 18 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147169043/ 5 (b) directing the respondents to pay for loss of physical or mental injury done since the date of marriage to till date and also for present litigation expenses @ 15,00,000/, Total amount claimed Rs. 28,00,000/, (c) directing the respondents to pay Rs. 30,000/ per month, (iv) Compensation and Damages Under Section 22 @ Rs. 28,00,000/ for harassment, mental torture, agony and ill treatment to the complainant, (v) An order or relief whereby directing the police to ensure safety of the complainant at her residence and to register an FIR against the respondents for criminal intimidation, threats to her life and property and also for outraging her modesty. 15. Vide order dated 15.05.2012, Ld. Predecessor directed to issue summons all the respondents except respondent no. 5. On receiving notice, Ld. counsel for respondents appeared before the court and expressed respondents willingness to contest the petition. The respondents were directed to file their replies with advance copy to the opposite party before NDOH. No reply was filed on behalf of respondents despite availing number of opportunities, therefore vide order dated 28.09.2012, right to file reply was closed and defence of respondents was struck off. The respondents preferred an appeal against the said order, which was allowed subject to cost of Rs. 6000/ to be paid to the complainant. Accordingly, respondents were allowed to file their replies on payment of cost to the complainant. 16. On completion of pleadings, matter was fixed for arguments on interim application. Vide order dated 06.02.2014, interim application of complainant was disposed off. Vide said order, respondent no. 1 was directed to pay a sum of Rs. 15,000/ per month as interim maintenance from the date of filing of the present CC NO. 59/1/12 PS: SUBZI MANDI KRITIKA JAIN VS. ANKIT JAIN 8/15 petition till its disposal. Subsequent thereto matter was fixed for complainant evidence. 17. In support of her case, the complainant has examined herself as CW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit, which is Ex.CW1/A, bearing her signatures at point A & B and also relied upon documents which are Ex. CW1/1 to Ex. CW1/13. The document Ex. CW1/ 8 was Deexhibited and marked as MarkX. Cross examination of CW1 was deferred as neither respondents nor their counsel appeared. Thereafter, vide order dated 25.02.2015, her cross examination was recorded as Nil Opportunity Given as despite availing opportunities, respondents did not cross examine her . 18. On closure of complainant evidence, matter was fixed for respondents evidence (RE) if any/ final arguments. The respondents did not lead any evidence in support of their claims. So much so, respondents and their counsel stopped appearing before the court. Keeping in view the conduct of respondents, opportunity to lead RE was closed. Subsequent thereto, final arguments were heard on behalf of the complainant. The respondents did not appear to tender their arguments. They were given liberty to file written arguments but no written arguments were filed.
